title: The Modern Philanthropist 2026
summary: Discover how different perspectives, relationships and expertise can help support more personal, strategic and impactful giving.
body_markdown:
From family and friends to professional advisers, peers and charities, many people can play a part in a donor’s philanthropic journey. Drawing on different perspectives and expertise can help donors shape their ambitions, navigate complexity and consider different approaches, with the potential to increase the impact of their giving.


Our research for The Modern Philanthropist 2025 explored the motivations, behaviours and barriers shaping giving among the UK’s high-net-worth individuals. This year, we go a step further, exploring who donors turn to as their philanthropy evolves, the roles different people can play and how working with others can support more purposeful giving.


## Who do donors turn to for support?


There is no single model for effective philanthropy.


Some donors prefer to make decisions independently. Others involve family, seek the perspective of peers, work closely with charities or draw on professional advisers for specialist expertise.


What matters is not having a large or formal philanthropy ‘team’, but understanding when another perspective, experience or area of expertise could be helpful.


### What role can family play?


For many donors, philanthropy is closely connected to family, values and legacy.


Involving family members can create opportunities to share perspectives, explore different priorities and develop a common sense of purpose. It can also raise important questions. Who should be involved? How should decisions be made? What happens when different generations have different ideas about what their giving should achieve?


Thoughtful conversations can help families navigate those differences while leaving room for individual interests and ambitions.


### Where can professional support add value?


Philanthropic decisions do not always sit neatly apart from the rest of a donor’s life.


A significant gift might intersect with tax, estate planning, investments, the sale of a business or wider questions about wealth and succession. Keeping relevant advisers informed can help donors consider philanthropy alongside their broader financial plans.


The opportunity extends beyond technical expertise. Advisers can help donors explore different possibilities, ask useful questions and introduce specialist philanthropic support where appropriate.


### What role do charities play?


Charities are not simply recipients of philanthropy. They bring valuable knowledge of the communities they serve, the challenges they are seeking to address and where funding can make the greatest difference.


Strong relationships can help donors deepen their understanding of an issue, while giving charities a clearer sense of a donor’s interests and intentions.


For donors who want to be effective partners, this can mean listening as well as asking questions, and recognising where charities themselves are best placed to determine how resources can be used.


## Finding the approach that works for you


There is no right number of people to involve in philanthropy, nor a single approach that will suit every donor.


For some, the right support may be informal. For others, particularly as their giving grows or becomes more complex, a more structured approach may be helpful.


The important question is not simply “Who should be on my philanthropy team?”, but “Who could help me at this point in my giving?”


That answer may change over time.
